events.what: An internal research version of Claude produces a proof that more than 67.2% of nontrivial zeta zeros are simple and on the critical line (previous record about 41.7%); announced by Anthropic and verified by Alpöge and Furman
events.ai_basis: A proof of these results was very recently produced by an internal research version of Claude developed by Anthropic and subsequently verified by Alpöge and Furman.

events.what: Lamzouri gives an independent human proof of the same bound (>67.25% simple and on the line, >83.62% distinct), crediting Claude's earlier result
Various preprints claiming full proofs or disproofs of RH (e.g. arXiv:2404.06306 in math.GM, a Zenodo 'Most Definitive and Comprehensive Disproof' posting)
events.credibility_reason: F5: landmark problem, no expert uptake, non-refereed math.GM category and repository postings, later work (Lamzouri 2026, Connes survey) still treats RH as open.

judgement.doubts: A bound on the proportion of zeros on the line counts as a bound on this bullet, so progress is right. Lamzouri's human proof is a bound at the same tier; the record says it 'reproduces and slightly extends' the result (67.25% vs >67.2%), which may just be the same bound stated to more digits. I did not treat it as superseding the AI bound: Lamzouri credits Claude's result as coming first. Even if it were read as superseding, the status would stay progress. The Anthropic PDF was never opened, and external endorsement by Conrey and Goldston rests on secondary reporting only.

corrections.why: other: 'bound' is not an AI-role value. Scope and AI role are separate questions, and the scope (bound) already gives the status progress. The basis quote says the proof 'was produced by an internal research version of Claude ... and subsequently verified by Alpöge and Furman', which is AI-generated mathematics checked by humans.

other: I kept this after weighing the record's competing_reading (open/no_change). A lower bound on the proportion of zeros on the critical line moves a quantity on this exact question, so it is scope bound, not variant.
